Generate and Format Covariate Labels for Forest Plots

generateCovNames.Rd

Dynamically constructs covariate names from a forest plot covariate data frame. If dfres is provided, it safely maps these generated labels directly onto the results data frame using the COVNUM relational key, returning the updated data frame.

It features an interactive two-step workflow: run with print_template = TRUE to generate a boilerplate mapping script in the console, then fill it out and pass the maps back in to append units, replace categorical labels, or format group headers.

With name_map, a covariate is named once and that name is used in every row label and in the group header: name_map = c(WTKGBL = "Weight") and unit_map = c(WTKGBL = "kg") label the rows "Weight = 58.3 kg" and "Weight = 126 kg", whatever percentiles the data give, and head the group "Weight". Without name_map the labels are "WTKGBL=58.3 kg", as before.

Categorical levels are named per covariate with level_map, e.g. level_map = list(SEXN = c("1" = "Male", "2" = "Female")). A level set to NA drops its row from the plot.

A set of 0/1 dummy covariates that together code one categorical covariate, such as GENO1N, GENO3N and GENO4N against a common reference genotype, is merged into one group with dummy_groups. Each dummy's 1 row is labelled with its level, and the 0 rows - one per dummy, all at the shared reference - become a single reference row. As the group is one GROUPNAME, onlySignificant in forestPlot() shows or hides it as a whole.

Every map is checked: a key given twice is an error, and with warn_unused, a key that matches no covariate or level in dfCovs - a typo, or a value that has changed with the data - is warned about rather than silently ignored.

A row's label is taken from the first of these that gives one: label_map, dummy_groups, level_map, name_map with label_format, and finally the column name and value, with the unit_map unit appended.

Usage

generateCovNames(
  dfCovs,
  dfres = NULL,
  unit_map = NULL,
  label_map = NULL,
  group_map = NULL,
  print_template = FALSE,
  name_map = NULL,
  label_format = "{name} = {value} {unit}",
  level_map = NULL,
  dummy_groups = NULL,
  sep = "_",
  warn_unused = TRUE
)

Arguments

dfCovs

A data frame containing covariate scenarios (must have a COVARIATEGROUPS column).

dfres

An optional results data frame generated by getForestDFSCM() or getForestDFemp(), or by PMXFrem::getForestDFFREM(). If provided, the function returns this data frame with the COVNAME and GROUPNAME columns updated and safely factored.

unit_map

A named character vector for appending units (e.g., c(WT = "kg")).

label_map

A named character vector for exact replacements (e.g., c("SEX=1" = "Male")). An NA entry drops the row, as in level_map.

group_map

A named character vector for replacing covariate group names (e.g., c("WT" = "Weight", "SEX" = "Sex")). A group not in group_map takes its name from name_map, so group_map is only needed when the group header should differ from the name in the row labels.

print_template

Logical. If TRUE, prints an R script template to the console and exits. The template has a name_map entry per covariate, a unit_map entry per continuous covariate and a level_map entry per categorical one. Whether a covariate is categorical is guessed from dfCovs (one-hot encoded, or only integer values from 0 to 9), so check the two lists. Blank entries are ignored, so the template can be passed back before it is filled in.

name_map

A named character vector of display names for the covariates (e.g., c(WTKGBL = "Weight", SEXN = "Sex")). When given, every row not matched by label_map is labelled with label_format, using the display name in place of the column name; covariates missing from it keep their column name. It also names the groups, see group_map.

label_format

The row label used with name_map. {name}, {value} and {unit} are replaced by the display name, the covariate value and the unit_map entry. Defaults to "{name} = {value} {unit}"; the space before an empty unit is dropped.

level_map

A named list with one entry per categorical covariate: a vector of labels named by level, e.g. list(SEXN = c("1" = "Male", "2" = "Female"), FOODDN = c("0" = "Fasted", "1" = "Fed")). A mapped level is labelled with its label alone. A level left out, or set to "", falls through to name_map, e.g. "Sex = 1". A level set to NA drops the row.

dummy_groups

A named list merging 0/1 dummy covariates into one group each. The name is the group header, and each entry is a list with levels, the label of each dummy's 1 row named by the dummy, and ref, the label of the single reference row kept from the dummies' 0 rows, e.g. list("2D6 genotype" = list(ref = "2D6 EM", levels = c(GENO1N = "2D6 UM", GENO3N = "2D6 IM", GENO4N = "2D6 PM"))). Leave ref out, or set it to NA, to drop the reference row as well.

sep

The separator between the covariate name and the level in the one-hot column names, as given to setupDfCovs(). When left out, it is read from dfCovs if setupDfCovs() made it, and is "_" otherwise.

warn_unused

Logical. Warn about map keys that match no covariate or level in dfCovs? Defaults to TRUE; set it to FALSE when sharing one set of maps between models with different covariates.

Value

If dfres is NULL, returns a character vector of formatted covariate names, one per row of dfCovs, with NA for a dropped row. If dfres is provided, returns the updated dfres data frame containing factored COVNAME and GROUPNAME columns, without the rows of dropped levels.

See also

setupDfCovs() for the covariate table, forestPlot() for the plot.

Examples

# 1. Create a synthetic forest plot covariate dataframe
dfCovs <- data.frame(
  COVARIATEGROUPS = c("WT", "WT", "SEX", "SEX"),
  WT = c(70, 90, -99, -99),
  SEX = c(-99, -99, 1, 2)
)

# 2. Create a synthetic results dataframe
dfres <- data.frame(
  COVNUM = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  PARAMETER = rep("CL", 4),
  VALUE = c(1.1, 1.3, 0.9, 1.0)
)

# 3. Define Translation Maps
name_map <- c(WT = "Body Weight", SEX = "Sex")
level_map <- list(SEX = c("1" = "Male", "2" = "Female"))
unit_map <- c(WT = "kg")
label_map <- c("SEX=1" = "Male", "SEX=2" = "Female")
group_map <- c("WT" = "Body Weight", "SEX" = "Biological Sex")

# --- Example A: Extract Character Vector ---
# Returns standard formatted strings for covariate names
generateCovNames(dfCovs, unit_map = unit_map, label_map = label_map)
#> [1] "WT=70 kg" "WT=90 kg" "Male"     "Female"  

# --- Example B: Relational Data Frame Mapping ---
# Safely mutates the data frame, adding locked COVNAME and GROUPNAME factors
dfres_updated <- generateCovNames(
  dfCovs,
  dfres = dfres,
  unit_map = unit_map,
  label_map = label_map,
  group_map = group_map
)

print(dfres_updated)
#>   COVNUM PARAMETER VALUE  COVNAME      GROUPNAME
#> 1      1        CL   1.1 WT=70 kg    Body Weight
#> 2      2        CL   1.3 WT=90 kg    Body Weight
#> 3      3        CL   0.9     Male Biological Sex
#> 4      4        CL   1.0   Female Biological Sex

# --- Example C: Name each covariate once ---
# Rows read "Body Weight = 70 kg" and "Male"; the groups are "Body Weight" and "Sex"
generateCovNames(
  dfCovs,
  dfres = dfres,
  name_map = name_map,
  unit_map = unit_map,
  level_map = level_map
)
#>   COVNUM PARAMETER VALUE             COVNAME   GROUPNAME
#> 1      1        CL   1.1 Body Weight = 70 kg Body Weight
#> 2      2        CL   1.3 Body Weight = 90 kg Body Weight
#> 3      3        CL   0.9                Male         Sex
#> 4      4        CL   1.0              Female         Sex

# --- Example D: Drop a row ---
# NA leaves the SEX = 2 row out of the plot
generateCovNames(
  dfCovs,
  dfres = dfres,
  name_map = name_map,
  level_map = list(SEX = c("1" = "Male", "2" = NA))
)
#>   COVNUM PARAMETER VALUE          COVNAME   GROUPNAME
#> 1      1        CL   1.1 Body Weight = 70 Body Weight
#> 2      2        CL   1.3 Body Weight = 90 Body Weight
#> 3      3        CL   0.9             Male         Sex

# --- Example E: Merge dummy covariates into one group ---
# Three 0/1 genotype dummies become one group with a single reference row:
# "2D6 EM", "2D6 UM", "2D6 IM" and "2D6 PM"
dfGeno <- data.frame(
  COVARIATEGROUPS = rep(c("GENO1N", "GENO3N", "GENO4N"), each = 2),
  GENO1N = c(0, 1, -99, -99, -99, -99),
  GENO3N = c(-99, -99, 0, 1, -99, -99),
  GENO4N = c(-99, -99, -99, -99, 0, 1)
)
generateCovNames(
  dfGeno,
  dfres = data.frame(COVNUM = 1:6, PARAMETER = "CL"),
  dummy_groups = list("2D6 genotype" = list(
    ref = "2D6 EM",
    levels = c(GENO1N = "2D6 UM", GENO3N = "2D6 IM", GENO4N = "2D6 PM")
  ))
)
#>   COVNUM PARAMETER COVNAME    GROUPNAME
#> 1      1        CL  2D6 EM 2D6 genotype
#> 2      2        CL  2D6 UM 2D6 genotype
#> 4      4        CL  2D6 IM 2D6 genotype
#> 6      6        CL  2D6 PM 2D6 genotype
